source_text: Hircus in eremum portat iniquitates. Christus tulit peccata in corpus suum. Amen.
thought_title: The scapegoat carries sins into the desert; Christ bore sins in his body
orientation: Origen is explaining the Day of Propitiation rite in Leviticus 16, where the goat sent into the desert carries away the people's iniquities, and he applies it to Christ.
pass_a_gloss: The goat carries iniquities into the desert. Christ bore sins in his own body. Amen.

choices.why: The subject is the scapegoat from the Day of Propitiation rite, so the definite article makes the reference clear.
The preposition in with accusative indicates motion toward, matching the ritual sending of the goat away.
The present tense is kept to match the source's vivid present, describing the ritual action.
The perfect tense indicates Christ's completed action in the past, distinct from the present of the goat's ritual carrying.
The source uses iniquitates for the goat's burden, distinct from peccata for Christ's, so the distinction is preserved.
The source uses peccata for what Christ bore, and the glossary gives 'sin' for peccatum, so the standard rendering is used.

bible_refs.note: The goat bearing iniquities into the desert reflects the scapegoat rite, where Aaron lays hands on the goat and it carries their iniquities into the desert.
Christ bore our sins in his body on the tree, matching 'Christus tulit peccata in corpus suum'.

pass_b_english: The goat carries their iniquities into the desert. Christ bore our sins in his own body. Amen.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'sins' generically, not 'our sins'; adds possessive not in Latin.
last_rejected.fix: Christ bore sins in his own body. Amen.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'peccata' lacks explicit possessive; 'our' is normal contextual rendering for Christian soteriological formula (1 Pet 2:24).
